name: Bosporus
note: Splits Istanbul in two; forms half of the Turkish Straits.
description: The Bosporus is the narrowest strait used for international navigation on Earth, and the only one that runs through the middle of a great city. For its thirty-kilometre length it divides İstanbul — Europe on one bank, Asia on the other — while carrying every ship that moves between the Black Sea and the wider oceans. That double role, city street and world seaway, has defined it for millennia: Byzantium, Constantinople, and İstanbul each grew rich commanding it. Its rules are set by treaty — the Montreux Convention of 1936 — and its traffic threads beneath bridges that since 1973 have stitched the two continents together.
